summary: Wall Street slipped on 12 Nov: the S&P 500 fell 0.35% to 7,592, the Nasdaq 0.39% and the Dow 0.36%, small caps fell 1.7%, and the VIX rose 6.9% to 18.7 as the 10-year yield climbed to about 5.10%. Nvidia fell 4.3% after its CEO resigned, while AMD (+5.9%) and Broadcom (+5.5%) rose; Taiwan and Korea funds fell 2.9% and 1.6%, and Asian markets were mixed on 13 Nov with US futures slightly higher. Brent rose 3.3% to $95.82 and WTI 2.6% after US comments on Iran, Henry Hub rose 3.9% and European gas jumped 8.1% to EUR 93.70, while gold fell 2.9% and copper 1.5%. The dollar firmed (yen near 159.7, euro down 0.4%), and in food and farm inputs Corteva dropped 24% on 12 Nov (cause not verified) and the Baltic Dry Index extended its run to 3,020.

climate.headline: NOAA: El Nino at second-strongest Aug-Oct level since 1950; one Atlantic hurricane so far
climate.detail: CPC's 9 Nov update put the Aug-Oct relative index at +2.0C, just behind 1997-98, and its 8 Oct outlook gave 70% odds of a historic event in Nov-Jan. The Weather Company notes only one Atlantic hurricane this season, the fewest since 1925.
climate.source: NOAA Climate Prediction Center (update 9 Nov; discussion 8 Oct 2026), summarised by Watchers.news 10 Nov 2026

climate.headline: China's National Climate Center: record El Nino to shape a warmer, wetter winter
climate.detail: The Centre expects above-normal temperatures and precipitation nationally for winter 2026-27, with more frequent cold waves, heavy snow risk in the north and significantly more rain in the south.
climate.source: China National Climate Center press conference, reported by CGTN 4 Nov 2026

climate.headline: Rhine at Kaub fell to about 20 cm on 2 November, far below the 77 cm low-water reference
climate.detail: German waterway gauge data showed 19-21 cm after levels above 50 cm days earlier; river cruise operators cancelled some departures. Rain upstream could help, but timing is uncertain.
climate.source: German waterway authority gauge data, reported by RusTourismNews 2 Nov 2026

climate.headline: COP31 leaders' summit: Ethiopia to host COP32; forest fund at $7.9bn of $10bn target
climate.detail: The Tropical Forest Forever Facility has about $7.9bn pledged against a $10bn startup goal, with Norway's $3bn conditional. The report on the summit did not cover Article 6 carbon-market sessions.
climate.source: Climate Home News, COP31 Bulletin Day 3, 11 Nov 2026
